title: Introduce Warmth Index Provisioner and Tenant Threshold Fence

description:
Motivation:
Many tenants experience intermittent cold-start penalties when dedicated capacity is thin and autoscalers react solely to short-term utilization spikes. This PR introduces a Warmth Index: a bounded, time-windowed score representing how recently and how frequently a tenant has been served by warm capacity. The provisioner uses Warmth Index plus headroom signals to bias allocations toward colder tenants while enforcing a tenant threshold fence that gates revocations to avoid thrash.

Design summary:
- WarmthIndex: rolling-window counter + decay producing a 0..100 index. Higher values mean the tenant has been actively served recently. Implemented in controlplane/provisioner/warmth_index.go.
- Provisioner controller: consumes warmth_index, target_headroom, and cluster capacity to prioritize prewarm actions and prevent preemption of recently cold tenants. See controlplane/provisioner/provisioner_controller.go.
- Tenant Threshold Fence: a safety mechanism that blocks eviction-caused capacity reclamation for tenants that fall below a configurable warmth threshold or when cooldown is active. Implemented as a coordination primitive with explicit fence_tripped telemetry.
- Fallbacks: when metricstore is unavailable or stale, provisioner falls back to EWMA of recent allocations and conservative headroom retention, documented in the controller.
- Telemetry and dashboards: expose warmth_index, fence_tripped, fence_cooldown_remaining, and recent_served_percentile. Dashboard JSON included.

Checklist (what this PR contains):
- [x] WarmthIndex calculation and unit tests
- [x] Provisioner controller and e2e smoke tests
- [x] Tenant threshold fence and cooldown TTL enforcement
- [x] Prometheus metrics and dashboard panels
- [x] Operator docs and sample helm values
- [x] CI pipeline additions for provisioner smoke test

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests cover rolling window edge cases and EWMA fallback behavior (pkg/util/timewindow tests).
- Integration smoke verifies that warm_preallocations are favored for low-warmth tenants and that fence prevents repeated eviction in a synthetic noisy workload.
- Ran canary in staging for 48 hours with simulated bursty tenants: observed 23% reduction in cold-start latency P95 for tenants that were previously penalized, and no increase in overall cluster peak usage beyond expected prewarm allocations.

Operator impact and rollout plan:
- Feature gate: provisioner.warmth_index.enabled (default: false). Operators can enable in values.yaml.
- Controlled rollout: enable in staging -> 10% production clusters -> full rollout.
- Rollback: disable feature gate to revert behavior immediately.

Config knobs exposed:
- warmth_index.window_seconds (default 1800)
- warmth_index.decay_rate (default 0.5)
- provisioner.prewarm_target_ratio (default 0.05)
- fence.cooldown_seconds (default 600)
- provisioner.metric_staleness_tolerance_secs (default 120)

Related work:
- ENG-4721: prewarm policy proposals
- ENG-4876: eviction smoothing and safety primitives
- SUP-1420: customer escalations showing repeated eviction loops for medium tenants

Notes and future work:
- Next PR will add a simulation harness to iterate on warmth weighting and cost regressions.
- Consider integrating ML-derived warmth predictors if simple heuristics saturate.
